title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 1981 manuscript of La Longue Marche, in the part on the section conjecture. K ⊂ L are fields of finite type over Q. E_L = E_L^{L̄} = Gal(L̄/L) is viewed as an extension of Γ = E_K^{K̄} = Gal(K̄/K), with geometric kernel π_{L/K}^{L̄} = Gal(L̄/LK̄). The problem is a birational (function-field) form of the section conjecture.

Part a) of the conjecture starts on the previous page. Any (germ of a) section s: Γ → E_L normalizes the inertia group I_V of a valuation V of L/K whose residue field is algebraic over K. This page completes the statement: V is uniquely determined by this condition, and in fact s comes from a section of the decomposition group N_V over E_K.

Part b). Let U be an 'elementary' model of L/K, i.e. built by successive elementary fibrations in hyperbolic curves (Artin neighbourhoods). Then sections of π_1(U) = E_U^{L̄} over Γ should lift to sections of E_L over Γ. In the image the verb seems to be 'se relèvent en', not 'se relient aux'.

b) can also be phrased through a valuation V of L/K and its centre on U. Grothendieck reduces to the case of a K-rational point x ∈ U and a section attached to x. There he conjectures:
(32) (E_L)^{Γ^0} = 1, i.e. the centralizer in E_L of s(Γ^0) is trivial for every open subgroup Γ^0 ⊂ Γ.

He then observes that, because Centr_Γ(Γ^0) = 1 (Gal_K of a number field has no nontrivial centralizers of open subgroups), (32) is equivalent to
(33) (π_{L/K})^{Γ^0} = 1, i.e. no nontrivial geometric element is fixed by Γ^0 under the action via s.
(33) should follow by dévissage, via elementary fibrations and exact sequences of fixed points, from the analogous statement already conjectured in relative dimension 1 (hyperbolic curves).

Margin. Grothendieck asks again whether N_V = Norm(Ī_V), i.e. whether the decomposition group is the normalizer of inertia. He wants the conjugacy classes of sections attached to a fixed V (inside the set X_{L/K} of section classes) to form fibres over the valuations. Those fibres should be described by H^1(E_K, Ī_V), a Kummer-type torsor, much like packets of cuspidal sections. He also writes down a formula relating the centralizer and normalizer data of a section to Ī_V, and mentions 'la question des [points?] géométriques'.

The next page studies Δ_V, the image of Ī_V in π_{U/K}, as an analogue of a 'groupe-lacet' (loop or tangential data). It does so using a normal-crossings compactification X ⊃ U and henselizations at points of D.
errors: The equivalence (32) ⇔ (33) is correct. Write g = a·s(γ) with a ∈ π_{L/K} and γ ∈ Γ. If g centralizes s(Γ^0), then γ centralizes Γ^0 in Γ, so γ = 1 and g = a ∈ π^{Γ^0}.

The dévissage is only sketched. One must check that fixed points pass to the projective limit over models U, and that the induced sections on each π_1(U) satisfy the curve statement even when x ∉ U (the section is then cuspidal). Both points are fine but not written down.

The 'relative dimension 1' statement is called a conjecture. For hyperbolic curves over number fields, the triviality of Γ^0-invariants of π_1^geo is in fact provable by weight/Mordell–Weil-type arguments together with the centre-freeness of π_1^geo. It is a standard fact in later section-conjecture literature (as best I recall), so here it is a lemma rather than a deep conjecture.

ideas.what: Birational section conjecture: sections of Gal_L → Gal_K come from decomposition groups of valuations of L/K with residue field algebraic over K, the valuation being unique
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983, Longue Marche 1981); studied by Koenigsmann (2005), Pop (2010), Stix (book 2013)
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche (1981 manuscript, circulated)

ideas.what: Sections of π_1 of an elementary model U lift to sections of the birational Galois group
ideas.modern_name: lifting of sections from π_1(U) to Gal_L / compatibility of section conjecture with birational version
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore consequence of the section conjecture; discussed by Stix
ideas.where_published: possibly in the Longue Marche transcription

ideas.what: Trivial centralizer of a section's image (32) and its reduction to trivial Γ^0-fixed points in the geometric group (33)
ideas.modern_name: sections are self-centralizing / no Galois-invariant elements in π_1^geo
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix (centralizer results for hyperbolic curves)

ideas.what: N_V = Norm(Ī_V): the decomposition group equals the normalizer of the inertia group
ideas.modern_name: self-normalizing decomposition groups in birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pop (local theory in birational anabelian geometry)

ideas.what: Sections attached to a fixed valuation V form a torsor under H^1(Γ, Ī_V)
ideas.modern_name: packets of cuspidal sections / Kummer parametrization of sections at a boundary

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly envisages fibring the set of section classes X_{L/K} over the valuations of L/K. The fibres would be parametrized by H^1(E_K, Ī_V), together with the question N_V = Norm(Ī_V). This is an early form of the description of birational sections as 'valuation + Kummer datum', later worked out for cuspidal sections of curves. The higher-dimensional birational version (valuations of rank > 1, Ī_V ≅ Ẑ(1)^r) is not systematically treated in the literature as far as I know.
missed.quote: À nouveau se pose la question si N_V=Norm(Ī_V) ... les fibres de X_{L/K} sur H^1(E_K^{K̄}, Ī_V)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a precise structural target (a fibration of section classes over the valuation space) for the birational section conjecture in higher dimension, beyond the mere existence of a valuation.

deep.surprise_reason: The birational section conjecture and the centralizer statements are known and attributed to Grothendieck's Faltings letter and Longue Marche. The margin's fibration of sections over valuations, with H^1(Γ, Ī_V) fibres, is a nice anticipation of later cuspidal-packet results but not clearly new. The (32) ⇔ (33) reduction is routine.
transcription_corrections: 'se relient aux sections de' is likely 'se relèvent en sections de' (sections of E_U lift to sections of E_L).
'Grothendieck [?] (pas Γ=E_K^{K̄})' is likely '(posant Γ = E_K^{K̄}) on conjecture encore, bien sûr'.
'considérons' after 'L sur K,' is probably 'quelconque' or a similar adjective.
'ce qui se concentre [?] pour le cas' is probably 'ce qui se ramène au cas'.
'Qui on peut y remplacer Γ^0 par Γ^0_{[?]}' is probably 'Ici on peut y remplacer Γ^0 par Γ^0 [ouvert / ⊂ Γ]...'; the end of the line is unclear.
'cat.[?] de type fini' on the previous page is 'corps de type fini'.
